rationale: ROUND 2, resubmit of corr 21c19c1f (REVISE, gated by prior_art_librarian's HIGH). THE GATING HIGH IS REFUTED BY THE LANDMINE'S OWN BODY, and the seat said so conditionally -- it wrote 'IF the landmine's full text says what its title fragment implies'. It does not. The entry is '`RegisterVerifier` is not a drain -- a completion verifier for a type born needs_human_review guards a door that type never walks through' (LANDMINES.md:13058). Its mechanism paragraph: 'there are TWO registries that look like one ... A type registered in the first and absent from the second has a verifier that can never run'. Its CHECK paragraph, verbatim: 'Born needs_human_review => the verifier needs a sibling entry in reviewRevalidators (delegate to the same verify function so the two doors cannot disagree -- revalidate_truncated_component.go is the worked pattern).' **That is precisely and only what edits 6-7 do**: the type is already in registry one (check_phantom_internal_links.go's init registers it); this adds the sibling entry in registry TWO, delegating to that same function, copying the named worked pattern. The landmine is not a warning against this change, it is the specification for it -- and its own worked case (truncated_component, bugs_open/325) is the same fix made four days earlier. Mechanically confirmed rather than argued: the sweep's loader selects `status IN ('needs_human_review','unresolved')` (revalidate_review_queue_action.go, and a LANDMINE footprint states that filter verbatim), so parked rows ARE what it reads. TWO SEATS FOUND REAL DEFECTS AND BOTH ARE FIXED IN CODE, not argued away. (1) render_guardian, MEDIUM -- my '3 publish paths' claim for seam 1 was OVERSTATED. `RerenderSitePagesAction` (rerender_pages_actions.go:214) appears in NO entry of GlobalActionRegistry -- checked with the landmine's own one-command test, `grep -n '"RerenderSitePagesAction"' registry.go` returns nothing. It is dead code and cannot be dispatched. **The corrected claim is TWO live publish paths through seam 1** (single-page rerender, and the initial build via deploy_page), plus seam 2. The call site stays -- it is where a revival would need it and it costs nothing -- but the coverage claim is now accurate. The seat was right and I had the evidence in front of me: no live agent has a rerender_site_pages step, which I measured in round 1 and failed to connect. (2) bug_historian, MEDIUM -- report-builder was to be LEFT OFF as 'not the measured harm'. The seat named that as the estate's recurring shape (one call site guarded, mechanism generic elsewhere) and it is right that 'turn it on later' is exactly the reasoning that leaves the other path live. **So I measured it instead of defending it: there are ZERO pages of page_type 'report' fleet-wide, and none of the 24 pages serving a dead anchor is one.** An empty population cannot regress, so migration 575 now turns report-builder ON as well (5 keys, not 4) and its $post$ gains an arm that RAISEs if ANY live step running a seam action lacks the key -- which also catches a sixth consumer appearing between enumeration and apply. The exception is gone rather than justified. (3) bug_historian, LOW -- the assemble seam's silent no-op on a missing site_id. Fixed: it now warns, and deliberately ONLY when the step opted in, because an un-opted-in step skipping is not an event. (4) guardian, MEDIUM -- failure isolation on the shared assemble seam, stated for THIS seam rather than inferred. Fixed with a test rather than a sentence: TestADatabaseFailureNeverFailsTheAssembly arms the mock to return a connection error and asserts the assembled HTML comes back byte-identical. (5) bug_historian, MEDIUM -- I asserted 079/097 are a different class WITHOUT READING 097, and its title ('cta_integrity_misses_card_links_to_unbuilt_pages') reads like my class. Read now. **The distinction survives but my reasoning for it was unearned, and 097's title is misleading about its own contents**: its six missed links are four 'never planned' (no pages row at all -- the phantom class) and two whose page EXISTS at a different url (/cases/thames-water vs the stored /blog/thames-water.html -- the rewrite class). Not one of the six is a pages row that exists and has never shipped. 097's actual defect is that the CTA check does not walk arrays of child objects inside content_data (info-card-grid keeps destinations at content_data.cards[*].link_url), so it is a DETECTOR-COVERAGE bug, not a target-class bug. Worth stating positively: this change works on rendered anchors, so it covers 097's SURFACE (card links) incidentally for the unbuilt class -- and its control arm is aimed at exactly the info-card-grid shape 097 names. It does not fix 097, whose content_data array walk is untouched. 049 also read: it is the fleet-wide broken-link census and its 'unbuilt pages' half is this class, which is why check_phantom_internal_links (049 mechanism 2) is the producer this change's drain serves. (6) prior_art, MEDIUM -- the archived_page_guard.go:38 role mapping was cited from a CODE COMMENT, which is not evidence. Verified at the config instead: page-build-handler's spawn_rerender_agent step is `{action: spawn_agent, config: {role: page_renderer, agent_type: page-rerender}, next_step: deploy_page}` and call_agent's findTopicsForRole resolves target_role by matching that spawn step's `role` field. So deploy_page does reach page-rerender, and seam 2 is still independently necessary because assemble_page is a different action on three different agents. (7) prior_art, MEDIUM -- existence of checks.VerifyUnbuiltInternalLinkResolved. It exists at discovery_checks/check_phantom_internal_links.go, registered by that file's own `init() { RegisterVerifier("unbuilt_internal_link", VerifyUnbuiltInternalLinkResolved) }`, signature `(ctx, *sql.DB, VerifyTarget, *zap.Logger) (VerifyResult, error)` -- which is what edit 6 calls. (8) editquality, MEDIUM -- the ratchet test file was not itemised. It is now edit 8 in its own right; it was always in the commit, but the plan could not be checked for it, which was the objection. (9) editquality, LOW -- PlannedPageRefusedAfterHours is DECLARED by edit 1 itself (a new const beside the predicate, value 48), named so the doc comment's threshold and the SQL cannot drift. (10) architecture + guardian + reuse + constitution, MEDIUM x4 -- the third-instance question. I declared it in round 1 and the seats are right that declaring is not disposing. The architecture seat's own recommendation is the action taken: 'approve this fix to proceed, but record on LNK-030 (or open a fresh RFC ticket) that this is now three instances, so it doesn't quietly become four.' Done in this round as edit 9: an amendment ON LNK-030 recording the third instance, and RFC_049 opened as the consolidation ticket, so the next reader of either finds the count rather than re-deriving it. I am not consolidating the three predicates inside a bug fix -- that is the scope veto shape the guardian seat exists to catch. (11) architecture, LOW + its 'missing' -- the optional-key budget was asked for by name. Run: `scripts/audit-optional-key-budget.sh` at HEAD. **assemble_page and rerender_single_page are NOT in the COUNTED population at all** -- they are among the 99 live actions with no ActionInputSpec, so their optional surface is unknowable rather than near budget; rerender_page_sections IS counted at 3 keys, over_budget false, and this change adds no key to it. `go test ./cmd/config-key-audit/` passes at HEAD. Noted honestly: the guidelines seat's observation that registering the key via RegisterActionInputSpec would make that census accurate is correct and is real debt; it is not taken here because declaring an input spec for assemble_page changes how EVERY key on that action is resolved, which is a bigger change than this fix and would arrive as a passenger. (12) debug_historian, MEDIUM -- no mechanical check named for the Go-before-config sequencing the plan itself flags. Named now and carried in the bug file's acceptance section: before applying 575, `kubectl -n ai-persona-system exec <pod> -- grep -aq "suppressUnshippedOutboundLinks" /proc/1/exe` on EVERY replica, with a control in the same breath (a string that must be absent and one that must be present) -- never `strings`, never a discovery grep. The 575 file's own $pre$ cannot check this, which is why it is a human step in the runbook and not a guard. (13) render_guardian, LOW -- suppression removes content with a log trail and no escalation at the point of removal. Accepted as stated and NOT changed: it matches RepairPageLinks' existing precedent for dead links, the item the escalation would file already exists (the type this change also drains), and filing a second item per suppressed anchor would re-create bugs_open/077's 'items whose handler has no remit'. Recorded rather than silently declined. UNCHANGED FROM ROUND 1: the mechanism, the predicate and its measurements, the two arms, the outbound-only placement and the opt-in default-OFF. Rebuilt and retested against a clean git archive HEAD overlay: go build ./platform/... clean, go test ./platform/orchestration/... all packages ok.

edits.rationale: UNCHANGED from round 1. Adds PageLinkRefusedPredicateFor to the build-axis predicate family -- the ONE home for 'would an anchor here 404 and is the page not arriving'. editquality's LOW is answered here: this same edit DECLARES `const PlannedPageRefusedAfterHours = 48` beside the predicate, named so the doc comment's threshold and the SQL cannot drift. The alias is REQUIRED and the bare form degrades to FALSE (suppress nothing), because the correlated subquery's unqualified `id` would bind to page_components.id inside the EXISTS and refuse every page.
edits.sketch:
+const PlannedPageRefusedAfterHours = 48
+func PageLinkRefusedPredicateFor(alias string) string {
+	if alias == "" { return "FALSE" }
+	q := alias + "."
+	return fmt.Sprintf(
+		"( (%[1]sdeployed_at IS NULL AND COALESCE(%[1]sbuild_status,'') = 'planned'"+
+		" AND %[1]supdated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '%[2]d hours')"+
+		" OR (%[1]sdeployed_at IS NULL AND COALESCE(%[1]sbuild_status,'') = 'needs_rebuild'"+
+		" AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM page_components pc"+
+		" WHERE pc.page_id = %[1]sid AND COALESCE(pc.rendered_html,'') <> '')) )", q, PlannedPageRefusedAfterHours)
+}

UNCHANGED from round 1. The site-level policy, a structural sibling of chrome_link_policy.go: same shape, same two degrade escapes, same fail directions. Returns (nil,false) on failed lookup, scan error, truncating row error, and on ZERO shipped pages -- the first-build escape, keyed on the SHIPPED-PAGE COUNT and never on the size of the refused set. Writes a durable CONTENT_LINK_SUPPRESSED_UNSHIPPED row naming every href; a skip writes writeLinkRepairSkipLog. reuse_agent's LOW (why a sibling rather than a parameterised shared policy) is answered on record: generalising chrome_link_policy.go would put a body-content caller inside a type whose own LANDMINE says its Allows() must never be read as a deployment proof, and the two policies deliberately use DIFFERENT predicates (chrome negates NeverDeployedPagePredicate; this uses the narrower refused floor) -- so a shared policy would need the predicate injected, which is the parameter that makes it two policies again. SHIPS WITH refused_link_targets_test.go, described here rather than itemised because the gate caps a plan at 8 files and one edit is one file -- the same treatment link_suppress.go's tests get, and the ratchet test STAYS itemised separately because that was editquality's actual objection (it sits in a different file from the registration it guards). SIX tests, and the two the council should look at: TestADatabaseFailureNeverFailsTheAssembly answers guardian's MEDIUM with a test rather than a sentence -- the mock returns 'connection reset by peer' on the policy lookup with the flag ON, and the assembled HTML must come back BYTE-IDENTICAL, so a DB error inside the shared assemble seam can neither propagate to the three consuming pipelines nor truncate the page. And TestSuppressionIsOffWithoutTheOptIn is the RFC_010 default-OFF proof, REWRITTEN after its first form was measured vacuous. The other four: the predicate lockstep, the zero-shipped-pages escape, the failed-lookup fail-open, and the seam-confinement source scan (also rewritten, after a value-reference mutant walked past its 'name(' match, and now carrying its own synthetic-line gone-blind test).

THE GATING HIGH OF ROUND 2, ANSWERED BY ITEMISING IT. Round 2 submitted the ratchet TEST and left the map registration itself in prose, so editquality correctly read the plan as shipping edit 6's function with no caller. The registration is this edit: one entry in reviewRevalidators, which is the exact 'sibling entry' the gating landmine of round 1 prescribes, and which also widens what the sweep LOADS (coveredItemTypes derives from this map, so the two cannot disagree). Both halves are in one commit, bb1e144b5. ⚠ THE PAIRED TEST LIVES IN A DIFFERENT FILE and is why round 2 itemised the wrong one: revalidate_review_queue_test.go's TestRevalidatorCoverageIsDeliberate is a deliberate ratchet that fired on this addition exactly as designed ('if that is deliberate, update this test and say why in the commit'); its `want` list gains the type together with the closer census written into the test's own comment, matching what all four earlier adopters did. It is not itemised separately only because the gate caps a plan at 8 files and this edit is the one whose absence was the HIGH.

ROUND 3: HARDENED ON debug_historian's TWO HIGHs AND ITS MEDIUM, all three closed in the file. (a) 'filters only on is_active, and four agent types carry TWO active rows while only the higher version loads at runtime'. MEASURED: all five target types carry exactly ONE active non-snapshot row today, so nothing is wrong now -- fixed anyway, because the day that stops being true nothing announces it. Every statement now keys on a temp table of DISTINCT ON (type) ... ORDER BY version DESC, i.e. the row that actually loads; the ROLLBACK keys the same way, because for an undo addressing a dormant duplicate is the WORSE direction (it reads as undone while the key stays live). (b) 'jsonb_set at {workflow,steps,render_page,...} is blind to sub_workflow-nested steps and create_missing will mint a dead top-level key'. The seat read my SKETCH, which showed only the render_page UPDATE; the FILE has three, with both nested paths spelled in full. But the underlying hazard is real and is now guarded: create_missing=true creates only the LAST key, so an absent parent `config` is a SILENT NO-OP returning the row unchanged. $pre$ now asserts the config PARENT at every path, not just the step -- verified 2026-08-23 that all five carry one, so the guard exists to make a future drift ABORT rather than write nothing and read clean. (c) MEDIUM, no snapshot before a live jsonb mutation on a table with heavy missed-snapshot history: added, snapshot_agent(type, reason) for every row the file touches, before it touches any. The 340/336 precedent skipped this and conceded it; a conceded omission is not a licence to repeat it.
